Forwarding usage export and a quick analysis. See attached pilotai_usage.csv — it contains token consumption by API key and timestamp. High-level observations:
- The primary eval key shows steady consumption until 07/15, then a burst pattern of short-lived sessions across ~12 distinct API keys tied to the same billing email domain.
- Several keys had small but frequent spikes at odd hours (02:00–04:00 PDT) consistent with scripted bulk calls.
- I pulled a list of related accounts that share device IP blocks and similar client metadata (attached suspicious-account-list.txt).

Given the multi-key pattern there’s potential for parallel pilot teams or account-sharing. Not definitive fraud, but worth an internal check before we issue more credits. Attaching files: pilotai_usage.csv, suspicious-account-list.txt.

-Ben

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: PilotAI usage & preliminary anomaly snapshot

Thanks for the data. Quick fraud triage:

1) Multiple API keys tied to the same corporate domain can be normal for multi-team pilots, but the clustering of client metadata (identical user-agent strings, near-identical request inter-arrival times) and the IP block overlap increase risk of scripted reuse.
2) The spike windows (02:00–04:00 PDT) align with a pattern we’ve previously seen where customers run parallel benchmark sweeps using ephemeral keys to avoid rate limits.
3) I cross-referenced the suspicious-account-list against past flagged accounts; two entities share device fingerprints with known multi-account aggregation behavior.

Recommendation: hold on issuing the 200K request. Offer a controlled 100K token grant with strict rate-limits and request that PilotAI consolidate to a single evaluation API key (we can issue a scoped key) for the extension period. Also request a brief attestation from their security lead that these are internal teams and not aggregated reseller traffic.

If PilotAI declines the scoped-key approach, escalate to deny and open an abuse review. I’ll create FRAUD-2027-154 and freeze any new trial top-ups until resolution.

-Rishi Malhotra
Lead Trust & Safety Analyst | Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia — quick update from our side after reviewing internal usage. I appreciate the ask and the context. We’re happy to support a short extension but need to put a couple of controls in place to protect both parties while the eval continues:

1) We can provide a one-time 100,000 token credit and extend the pilot window by 7 days.
2) We will issue a single scoped evaluation API key for PilotAI to use across both product teams. That key will include rate limits to prevent high-concurrency sweeping.
3) As a condition, please have your security lead reply to this thread confirming all traffic is internal to PilotAI (no reseller/partner aggregation).

If you can accept those conditions I’ll approve the credit and push the extension through today. If not, we’ll need to decline the larger 200K request while we run a deeper abuse review (Rishi is on copy and has opened an internal ticket).
